en: The turning play of Poush and Phalgun, rocked on a swing of tears and laughter,
in its midst, lifelong, I shall carry my tray of songs —
Is this your pleasure — is that why you hung this garland on me,
steeped in the fragrance of melody?
Is that why my sleep has fled, why the dam of my mind has broken,
why waves of a mad wind rise in the forest of undying pain,
and all the dark and light of my days and nights is trembling!
Is this your pleasure — is that why you hung this garland on me,
steeped in the fragrance of melody?
No nest was built for the night, and the day's work is left flawed,
yet in this service without work I find no release.
Where in all the wide world, alas, is peace for me?
It is unrest that strikes — and so the veena plays.
Forever the fire of heart-searing song will burn —
Is this your pleasure — is that why you hung this garland on me,
steeped in the fragrance of melody?
Master of melody, grant us the initiation of song —
we are beggars for melody; this is the alms we ask.
The stream of the Mandakini, the morning star of dawn,
the golden champak — all learned that melody, whispered ear to ear.
Filling my heart with your melody,
I will go where discord plays unending.
Where the rush of clamor wakes a rising whirl,
there let my veena take its test.
Where the stream of your melody comes pouring, there on its shore —
will you give me a nest at one edge?
I will hear that sound with my ears,
I will fill my soul with that sound,
and with that sound, again and again, I will string my heart's veena.
My silent hours, in your melody upon melody,
will brim like honey within the flower.
When my day is done,
when the night grows dark,
the stars of song will bloom in my heart, row upon row.
How do you make your song, O master —
amazed, I listen, I only listen.
The light of melody covers the world,
the wind of melody moves along the sky,
breaking through stone, rushing in restless haste,
the sacred river of melody flows on.
I think to sing in that very strain,
but in my throat I cannot find the tune.
What I long to say — the words stumble as I speak;
defeated, my soul weeps;
into what snare have you cast me,
weaving a net of melody on every side of me!
For all the songs I ever sang to you
I ask no gift at all in return.
If you should forget that song, then forget it if you must,
when the stars rise on the shore of the evening sea,
when in your court I come to my end —
these few days only, these few strains of mine.
How many of your songs you sang to me —
how will you ever forget that?
That thought, O poet, will come back to your mind
on rain-loud nights, in the breeze of spring —
only this much hurt pride remains my own —
can you forget that you beguiled my soul?
You set the fire of melody alight in my soul —
this fire has spread to every place.
On every branch of the dead trees
the fire dances, beat upon beat,
it lifts its hands to the sky — toward whom?
All the stars of the dark keep gazing, amazed;
from somewhere a mad wind comes rushing.
In the heart of midnight this stainless
golden lotus has bloomed —
who knows what power the fire holds.
Your veena, within my mind —
sometimes I hear it, sometimes I forget, sometimes I do not hear it at all.
When the sky shivers into song
and keeps whispering its secret words into the ear of the earth,
suddenly amid it a fierce clamor rages —
in my mind the unbound dreams come throng on throng.
O veena-handed one, in your court
my restless heart, gone mad, plays out of tune.
Your voice — sometimes I hear it, sometimes I do not hear it at all.
I was walking through your lotus grove
when midway the restless breeze beguiled me from the path.
Your melody wakes on the night of spring,
your melody on the ashoka bough, in the dawn-red hue of pollen.
Riding that melody I long to drift, my mind forgetting itself,
with the honeybee of humming, hurrying wings.
Why does the mist wrap me in its veil —
the dark makes the light turbid, and my eyes die of shame —
Your voice — sometimes I hear it, sometimes I do not hear it at all.
Your eyes have told me, again and again, to sing my song.
In flower after flower, in star after star,
they have said it — by what secret sign? —
on the borderland of day and night, in grey light and in darkness.
Why I do not sing — what can I say?
Why this restlessness of mine —
the words hide inside the pain, and I lose the tune on the shoreless deep.
Gliding by on the deep current, you have called me from your boat.
You have called in storm and tempest,
in the thunder-song of the mute clouds,
you have called me toward death, in the wild torrent of the monsoon night.
Why I do not go — do you not know?
With my eyes turned toward you,
I sit at the landing on the shore — where is my path across the sea?
Formless One, your word —
may it bring freedom into my body, into my heart.
Your everlasting festival is the world's festival of lamps —
I am only its lamp of clay — kindle its flame,
your will, ablaze with light that never dies.
As your spring wind goes writing its lines of song
in color upon color, on blossom and leaf, from wood to wood, on every side,
so fill the center of my being with your breath;
filling its emptiness, let melody make it blessed —
and may your right hand make its hindrance holy.
Song upon song, let your bond be broken —
in the dark of the imprisoned word a weeping wakes.
Where in the World-Poet's heart the veena of the universe plays,
let your life fall prostrate there in the stream of melody.
Your rhythm, breaking, breeds conflict in the soul,
so within and without, strain does not meet with strain.
The tune-lost soul is a dire barrier — that is the storm, that is the maze —
You who forgot your song, take your song back — let that peril flee.
Your smile falls upon my melody,
as the sun's rays come and sway on wave after wave.
Day and night I too wander in search of your melody,
then suddenly, who knows when, your flute beguiles this mind.
All my work is left undone, all my lessons I have shirked;
meaning to catch you in my song, I wander off, absent-hearted;
I love to be caught in your song.
My day is passing into the evening hour
in matching my tune to your melodies.
The one string of my one-stringed lute cannot bear the ache of song;
again and again I have lost to you in this game —
in matching my tune to your melodies.
This string of mine is tuned to melodies near at hand;
that flute plays far away.
Can everyone join in at that shore of the play of song,
to cast the net of ragas on the ocean of the world's heart —
in matching my tune to your melodies?
Beyond the bounds of life and death,
O friend of mine, you stand.
In this lonely sky of my heart
your great throne is veiled in light;
with what deep hope, what deep-felt thrill,
I gaze toward it with both arms outstretched.
The silent night, in worship at your feet,
has spread her weight of darkened hair.
Today what song, flooding all the world,
has come down from your veena!
The world dissolves into the ringing of the tune;
in the ache of song I am lost.
Those who tell of you with words
only weave fence after fence of words, faction upon faction.
One man's words the next
cannot understand,
the more they explain, the more the load of words keeps growing.
Those who leave words behind and only play the tune —
in their tune all meet as one, the near and the far.
Whether one understands or not,
no one stops to ask;
their ache arrives to rest beneath your feet.
In the solitude beneath your waterfall.
who knows at what moment this clay pitcher of mine overflowed.
There the sun goes down behind the hills,
the wild geese fly off into who knows what sky —
and I, in the murmuring of this tender stream,
keep my ear bent in silence, lost in thought,
In the solitude beneath your waterfall.
By day I go about seeking whatever I need;
met or unmet, I will fret for it no more.
After long wandering all day, at the day's end
I have come to the country beyond all wanting;
today, come to the shore of the boundless stream, I will take
that treasure you give, overflowing all need,
In the solitude beneath your waterfall.
From the shore I set loose my boat of song,
set it afloat in mid-sea with its sail raised.
Where the koel calls beneath the shade —
not there;
where the village bride comes down to the water —
not there;
but where the blue play of death rises swaying —
there I set loose my boat of song.
Now, veena, you and I — we are alone;
in the dark, no matter if we see no one.
The flower one gathers from the bough of the grove —
this is not that flower;
the flower that sways on the vine at the window —
this is not that flower —
toward the sky-filling flowers of melody, all directions lost —
that way I set loose my boat of song.
Of you I beg this boon — that I may wake from death
in the melody of song.
That the moment my eyes open, like the nectar of a mother's milk,
new life may fill me full — in the melody of song.
There every tree and blade of grass
rises like a song out of the earth's flute.
There the light comes bringing
the sky's message of joy,
and roams about within the heart — in the melody of song.
Why do you call me, all of you? My mind will not obey.
I find no time — song upon song.
People ask me the way — but does the way ever meet my eye?
and I drift toward whatever side — song upon song.
Give me leave, then; blame my faults — I will not hear.
My mind floats away — song upon song.
Today is the hour of blossoming; today the sky holds a fair of colors,
and every side is pulling at me — song upon song.
You stand on the far shore of my song —
my melodies find your feet; you I never find.
The wind is blowing — ah me! — keep your boat tied no longer;
come, come across into the middle of my heart.
With you this play of song is a play across the distance,
and all day long the flute is played in pain.
When will you come yourself, take up my flute and play,
in the deep dark of the silent night, brimming with joy?
In the royal palace a flute is playing the strain of day's end.
I walk the road, and a traveler asks, 'What gift do you carry?'
What do I own worth showing to them all?
With me I carry only these few songs.
At home I have many people's minds to please —
many flutes, many cymbals, many an array.
But coming to my beloved I took only this song in my throat,
to make it a garland for that neck and give it worth.
Wake, wake, O music, wake — set the sky of the mind in waves,
in the heart's bowered canopy, deep in delight, atremble with love.
Let your seven notes, their bonds unloosed, go ranging through the universe;
let them proclaim their joy in the realms of sun and moon and stars.
Strain upon strain, soul upon soul, weave the garland of paradise.
Fill the courtyard of the sky with the song of his praise.
The song I came here to sing —
that song has not been sung;
even now I only practice the tune; mine is
still only the wanting to sing.
That tune has not come to me,
those words have never been bound;
only in the middle of my soul there lives
the restlessness of song.
Still that flower has not bloomed — only
a wind has been blowing.
I have not seen his face, I
have not heard his voice;
only from moment to moment I hear
the sound of his footsteps.
Past the front of my door that one
keeps coming and going.
Only the seat has been laid out
through the whole of the day —
in the house no lamp has been lit — him,
how shall I call?
I stay on with the hope of finding — him
I have never found.
I stay here only to sing your song —
in your world-court grant me this little place.
In your world, Lord, I have been of no use —
this workless life does nothing but ring in tune.
At night, in the silent temple, is your worship;
command me then to sing, O King.
At dawn, when across the sky the veena rings in golden strains,
let me not be left far off — grant me this honor.
I spread the seat of song's melody beside the road.
O traveler, you will come and sit again and again.
There is your morning bird, calling and calling without end;
when you come by the ferry of dawn-light to the landing shore,
stand at my door within my morning song.
This morning the shadow of the clouds lies fallen across the wood,
and water brims in the corner of the sky's blue eye.
Today you have come in new attire, past the palms at the field's end —
do not slip away at once on your secret rounds.
Stand in the rain-dark of my clouded song.
When I forget the tune and wander about in nothing but work,
the reproach of your eyes strikes me in the breast.
The soaring sky, the generous earth, brimming with nectar of blue and green,
melt into the distance — their touch cannot be had —
the reproach of your eyes strikes me in the breast.
On wind after wind of that road of melody, the universe
keeps my heart restless with its coming and going.
I seat you in such a spot as I have nowhere else in the world —
yet within myself I lose the seat where union might be —
the reproach of your eyes strikes me in the breast.
